name: atc
title: atc
description: Every Claude Code session on every machine an atc server lists, in the panel and on the bar: which ones need you, a chat to read and answer each, permission prompts allowed or refused, new sessions in any folder on any machine, earlier conversations resumed, and what each session made.
author: pal

settings.label: atc server
settings.description: The address of your atc server. Empty uses the one atc login saved on this machine.

settings.label: Token
settings.description: What atc token prints on the server. Empty uses the one atc login saved; a server that trusts your tailnet needs none. Kept in the OS keychain.

settings.label: Open a session in
settings.description: Where Open in a terminal app goes. Auto runs atc attach in a terminal when the atc command is on this machine, and opens atc's web page otherwise.

settings.label: Terminal
settings.description: Which terminal atc attach opens in; Auto takes the first one installed.

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.description: Every session atc lists, the ones that need you first: the machine, folder and branch, what it is doing or asking to run, the context it holds; the pane is your last message and its last reply.

keys.title: Open the chat (Tab, a message, Enter sends it first)
Allow what it asks to run
Say no, or interrupt a working turn
Open in a terminal app (atc attach)
Outputs: the servers, files and links it made

chat.title: Chat
chat.description: One session as a chat that follows it live: the conversation, what it is doing now, a permission prompt with its two keys, and a message field. Opened bare, the session that needs you most.

keys.title: Send the message (a stopped session is resumed first)
Attach the clipboard: text into the message, a picture or files uploaded with it

terminal.title: Terminal
terminal.description: A session's own terminal inside pal, Claude Code's screen as atc attach shows it, in the panel's colours: type into it, scroll it, answer any prompt. A stopped session is resumed first. Opened bare, the session that needs you most.

keys.title: Send Escape (ctrl+[ too): interrupt, say no; Escape itself goes back
Fit the terminal to this window

new.title: New Session
new.description: Start Claude Code in a folder on any machine atc lists: the folders you used lately, then those under atc's roots; Tab to type the first message and a name.

keys.title: Start it in a new git worktree

history.title: Earlier Conversations
history.description: Past conversations on every machine, newest first, found by title, folder or what you asked: read one, or resume it in the background.

keys.title: Read it (a message typed after Tab resumes it)

outputs.title: Outputs
outputs.description: What your running sessions made: the servers they started, the files they wrote or read, the links they gave.

needs_you.description: Sessions waiting on you to allow something or answer

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.description: A count per state in its colour (red needs you, amber your turn, blue working), an alarm while one needs you; the popover lists them by state on every machine, opens a chat, allows or refuses a prompt, starts a new one.

keys.title: Allow what it asks to run
Say no, or interrupt a working turn
Open in a terminal app (atc attach)
Move the cursor (down, j, k too; a click sets it)

session.description: A session id, its background id, or words of its title; absent, the one that needs you most

send.description: Send a message to a session

session.description: A session id, its background id, or words of its title

file.description: A file to upload with it (repeat for several)

host.description: The machine, when atc lists several

store.tagline: Your Claude Code sessions on every machine, through atc
features: Every session on every machine your atc server lists, the ones that need you first, with what each is doing or asking to run
A chat per session that follows it live: read the conversation, type a message, `cmd+y` allows a prompt, `cmd+.` says no or interrupts
A session's own terminal inside pal (`cmd+o`): Claude Code's screen live in the panel's colours, to type into, scroll and answer anything
A bar item counting sessions by state, an alarm while one needs you; its popover answers them without opening pal
Start Claude in a folder on any machine, or a new worktree, with the first message typed in the bar
Earlier conversations from every machine, read or resumed in the background
The servers, files and links a session made, one Enter from open; the clipboard attached to a message with `cmd+shift+v`
Uses the server and token atc login already saved, so a machine with the atc command needs no setup

The pane: what it asks, your last message and its last reply; the machine, folder, model and context below
Enter opens the chat: the conversation live, the command it asks to run with cmd+y to allow and cmd+. to say no, a field to reply
New Session: a folder on any machine, the first message typed after Tab
⌘K on a session: allow, say no, open it in a terminal or atc's page, its outputs, pin, park, rename, stop
On the menu bar: how many sessions need you, are your turn and are working, an alarm while one needs you
A click opens the popover: every session by state on every machine; Enter opens its chat, y allows, i says no
The chat in the popover: what it asks and the conversation, answered without opening pal
On sketchybar: the three counts in red, amber and blue
